source: General LIBERO manipulation lessons, stated in terms of the current RGB-D views and robot proprioception.

lessons.trigger: Images show the fingers aligned around the intended grasp surface.
lessons.strategy: Use one deliberate close and inspect after lifting. A closed jaw alone does not establish retention. Select the next local instruction from current visual and proprioceptive evidence: a visibly separate object calls for pick/grasp before carrying-dependent placement. Do not put held/holding into a local policy prompt based only on closure or proximity. When occluded, inspect or restage using current public views rather than assume retention. Pure-code execution remains available.

lessons.trigger: Visible objects obstruct a direct approach.
lessons.strategy: Use a visible clear approach, lift relatively before translating when justified by the images, and inspect ambiguous clearance.

lessons.trigger: The visible grasp barely overlaps the object edge.
lessons.strategy: Adjust a small relative offset from the current depth surface while keeping visible supporting surfaces clear.

lessons.trigger: Images show interrupted pushing with little object movement.
lessons.strategy: Maintain the intended visible contact during a bounded stroke and inspect progress. Hidden contact forces are unavailable.

lessons.trigger: A move produces little measured robot displacement or an occluded view.
lessons.strategy: A completed motion command is not evidence that its waypoint was reached. Compare public positional progress with the current RGB-D view; re-localize and adjust a visible local route or posture before repeating an unreached approach. Do not assume a commanded lift created clearance. Reserve a local vla_act attempt for a current, visually supported contact setup; do not infer contact from residual error.
Prefer short motion plans and reuse approved recipes. Camera and model waiting time does not spend simulation steps.

lessons.trigger: The natural-language goal asks to move each, both, or several visible objects.
lessons.strategy: Reuse a transfer sequence for each requested natural-language clause, but rebind the source, support and relation from current RGB-D each time. Analytic actions can stage and transport; a single local vla_act contact attempt must be followed by fresh visual reassessment in an available planning revision. Pure-code transfers remain valid. Two default bound_transfer calls (236 each) exceed 400; allocate supported phase_steps within remaining_steps and do not cache instance coordinates or numbers.

lessons.trigger: The requested drawer opening and its handle are visible in the current configured views.
lessons.strategy: Select a current-image contact on the visible handle, maintain contact through a short bounded pull, and inspect the drawer afterward. Never infer a hidden joint axis or use simulator geometry.

lessons.trigger: A visible door or surface must be closed, pushed, or pressed.
lessons.strategy: Use a short contact-preserving stroke whose direction is supported by the current image, then inspect visible progress. Do not infer a hinge axis, contact force, or hidden completion state.

lessons.trigger: A narrow or handled object needs a grasp and its shape is visible.
lessons.strategy: Choose the gripper closing axis from the object's current visible shape. If the handle or narrow cross-section is ambiguous, use another configured view before selecting an approach; do not use historical world coordinates or simulator yaw.

lessons.trigger: The target or approach is obscured in one configured camera view.
lessons.strategy: Inspect another currently available configured RGB-D view and reselect from that fresh evidence. Do not substitute hidden poses, joint states, or old coordinates.
